characters.continuity: J.R.R. Tolkien's Middle-earth writings (The Silmarillion, The Lord of the Rings, and related legendarium texts)
characters.summary: Varda is the Queen of the Valar, dwelling in Valinor, and is the mightiest of the Valier. She kindled the stars, holds supreme command over celestial light, and is feared and hated above all other Valar by Morgoth because her light repels him.

techniques: Radiant divine light projection against darkness
Queen of the Valar who kindled the stars
Light that the powers of darkness fear: Ungoliant shrank from her eyes

mechanisms: Absolute purity and divine separation from mortal weapons
Not established by the cited source

weaknesses: No battle record described in the cited sources
mobility: Transcendental flight and presence across Eä
limitations: Bound to Valinor and the divine decrees of Eru Ilúvatar regarding direct physical intervention in Middle-earth

sources.supports: Identity, role as Queen of the Valar, kindling of the stars, and Morgoth's fear of her.
Kindles the first stars; spouse of Manwë; Melkor hates her most.
Ungoliant feared the eyes of Manwë and Varda and consumed light from Varda's wells.

feats.claim: Kindled the stars of the firmament and gathered the silver dews from the vats of Telperion to make new stars.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Beginning of Days

characters.earlierSummary: Varda is the Queen of the Valar, dwelling in Valinor above Ilmen. She wields supreme light and power, shaping the stars and hearing all sounds made within Eä, and her name is invoked as a supreme defense against darkness.

characters.summary: The Witch-king of Angmar is the chief of the Nazgûl and the most powerful servant of Sauron. He wields terrifying aura-based dread, dark sorcery that can break physical structures and weapons, a Morgul-blade, and a flaming sword, operating as a fearsome mounted and airborne commander.

Broke the gate of Minas Tirith; destroyed the kingdoms of Arnor

mechanisms: Undead wraith physiology immune to normal physical weapons

weaknesses: Vulnerable to blades forged with specific westernesse enchantments combined with unique lineage circumstances (e.g., Barrow-blade wielded by a woman and a hobbit)
Put to flight by Glorfindel at Fornost
Merry's Barrow-blade broke his protection and Éowyn killed him
Bound to Sauron through his Ring

characters.summary: Yavanna is the Valië of Earth and growth, mother of all things that grow in Arda. She commands immense nature magic, bringing flora and forests to life, singing the Two Trees into being, and conceiving the Ents to protect her beloved trees from fell creatures.

techniques: Not established by the cited source

mechanisms: Protection by other Valar such as Aulë and Oromë
Divine resilience as one of the Valar

weaknesses: Deep grief and vulnerability to the destruction of living plants and trees by fire or axes
mobility: Divine presence and travel across Arda
limitations: Cannot restore the Two Trees once drained by Ungoliant without the remaining light of Silmarils
Cannot restore the Two Trees of Valinor once their light was drained by Ungoliant without the light of the Silmarils.

sources.supports: Identity as Valier of growing things, creation of the Two Trees, and conception of the Ents.

feats.claim: Sang the Two Trees of Valinor (Telperion and Laurelin) into existence from the earth.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Beginning of Days

feats.claim: Conceived and petitioned for the creation of the Ents and the Eagles to guard living things against the incursions of Morgoth's creatures.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of Aulë and Yavanna

Specific combat engagements or offensive spellcasting outside of creation and life-giving.
